stance_text: Watch — the renewables write-downs are nearly finished, but $71 already pays for most of a recovery the Street expects in one year and this report expects to take until 2028–2029
lens_text: FY2029 company-adjusted diluted EPS x exit P/E (three-year value, undiscounted); adjusted EPS adds back intangible amortization and stock compensation, so each multiple is also stated on GAAP EPS

bear.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $3.43 ($2.57 GAAP): revenue +1%/yr from an estimated $7.00B FY2026 to $7.21B, GAAP op margin 3.6%, interest $58-60M, tax 31% (add-backs taxed at the same rate), 53.5M shares; x 10x adjusted (13.3x GAAP, near the top of the 2018-2023 range)

base.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $5.92 ($5.02 GAAP): revenue +7.5%/7.0%/6.5% to $8.58B, GAAP op margin 4.3%/4.6%/4.8%, interest $52M/$48M/$44M, tax 29%, 52.0M shares; x 13x adjusted (15.3x GAAP)

bull.basis: FY2029 adj EPS $7.84 ($6.92 GAAP): revenue +13.5% in 2027 to $7.95B then +10%/yr to $9.61B, GAAP op margin 5.6%, interest $50M/$45M/$40M, tax 28.5%, 51.5M shares; x 17x adjusted (19.3x GAAP)

horizon_text: FY2029 (year ending December 31, 2029) adjusted EPS at an exit P/E, undiscounted

deviation_from_street.reason: Timing, interest and multiple: the Street has FY2027 adjusted EPS at $5.32, a near-full return to 2025's $5.62 in one year; this call has $4.59 in 2027 and $5.28 in 2028 because renewables revenue is falling (~$2.1B in 2026 vs ~$3.0B in 2025), Energy carries underused crews, and interest is running near $57M a year after the PayneCrest debt. It also uses a 13x adjusted exit (15.3x GAAP) and puts 30% on a bear case after three guidance cuts in six months. Street targets are one-year values; this is a three-year undiscounted value.

thesis: The six loss-making solar projects are nearly finished, so 2026 is the trough, but full recovery to 2025's ~5.4% operating margin takes until 2029 because renewables volume is shrinking, and higher interest and amortization keep EPS a year behind; on that path adjusted EPS reaches ~$5.90 and the stock is worth ~$77 at 13x, about 2% a year from $71.
consensus_view: Sixteen analysts (11 Buy-rated) average a $100.47 target on FY2027 adjusted EPS of $5.32, a near-full snap-back to 2025; the market at $71.24 pays 13.4x that number, discounting the recovery modestly rather than doubting it.
variant_view: The Street's FY2027 rebound is about a year early: Q3 Energy revenue fell 17.6% even with PayneCrest, management describes solar new work as slow to start in every 2026 release, the Q4 guide implies only $0.59-0.74 of adjusted EPS, and Q3 interest annualizes near $57M; this call has FY2027 adjusted EPS of $4.59 against the Street's $5.32 and reaches the Street's number only in FY2028, so the stock is fair rather than cheap.

Revised after independent review (grade B): FY2026 revenue base, interest, add-back tax rate and base exit multiple changed; fair value fell from $81.23 to $75.40. See review.

low_score_reasons: valuation: the exit multiples come only from the company's own pre-2024 history, when it was a pipeline-heavy business, with no peer check; the base 14x adjusted (16.6x GAAP) is above every 2018–2023 year-end P/E and is described as 'between the eras' rather than derived; interest ($38–45M) and the 25% tax rate on add-backs are both too favorable against the Q3 run-rate and the company's own reconciliation; and the -19% gap to the Street compares a 3-year undiscounted value with 1-year targets, so the real disagreement is larger than it looks.
review.counter_case: On the call's own numbers this is an Avoid, not a Watch. The base case needs GAAP operating margin back to about 5.3% before amortization, a level the report admits was reached only in 2024–2025, and a 16.6x GAAP exit multiple above every 2018–2023 year-end (8.9–14.3x); at that range's 12.8x median, base FY2029 GAAP EPS of $5.16 is worth about $66, below $71.24. Meanwhile nine-month operating cash flow was $8.9M, the balance sheet went from $65.6M of net cash to $580.8M of net debt, Q3 interest of $14.3M is running near $57M a year against the $38–45M modeled, and the board has just authorized $250M more of buybacks. Put 30% on a -48% bear and the honest expected return is near zero.
review.response: Accepted most of it. Changes: interest re-based on the Q3 run-rate (base $52M/$48M/$44M, bear $58-60M, bull $50M/$45M/$40M); add-backs now taxed at each case's effective rate, matching Schedule 3 ($24.6M on $73.7M); FY2026 revenue base lowered from the $7.07B consensus to $7.00B because the Q4 guide implies a weak quarter; base exit multiple cut from 14x to 13x adjusted (15.3x GAAP); variant view corrected from 'two years early' to 'about a year early'; factual fixes to the Energy margin vs target range, PayneCrest backlog date, MSA backlog wording and the bear multiple's place in the historical range. Fair value fell from $81.23 to $75.40 (+1.9% a year), base from $85.53 to $76.96, bear to $34.26, bull to $133.20. The report now states that at the old 12.8x GAAP median the base is worth about $64. Not changed: the stance stays Watch because the rule gives Watch at +1.9% a year, and the base keeps a multiple one point above the 2018-2023 range because Utilities MSA work (backlog +27% this year) is a larger share of the mix than in the pipeline years; no peer multiples were captured to test that. The weights stay 30/50/20: the counter-case's near-zero return is close to what the revised numbers say, and it is inside the Watch band rather than below it.
